newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes remain weak, diffs listless.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes remain weak, diffs listless.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices remained weak late Tuesday, with differentials for Alaskan crude listless on weak demand.

Traders said crude supply was ample in PADD 5 storage, with stocks 3.6 million over year-ago levels, according to inventory data released Tuesday from the American Petroleum Institute. PADD 5 crude stocks stood at 68.4 million barrels, down 649,000 from the previous week.
Buyers said they expected little spot dealing with a industry function planned for the later half of the week and most refiners balanced.
Also, steep gains on Monday's overnight ACCESS put November crude at a new post-Gulf War high of $25.72. That left buyers concerned about profit margins on Tuesday.
After-hours trade showed November crude resuming its upward climb, with prices up as much 16 cents on ACCESS Tuesday.
Cash West Texas Intermediate (WTI) followed NYMEX lower, shedding five cents to hit $25.30/25.40 a barrel.
Outright prices for ANS eased to $23/23.30, with deltas steady at $2.30 less November WTI.
ANS Buyers bid around $2.50 under November WTI, while a major producer continued to offer at $2.10.
Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
California heavy crudes rose 15 cent with an increase in Texaco's posted prices on October 14. Kern River crude reached $17.30/17.50 a barrel.
Values for Wilmington crude increased to $18.65/18.75 a barrel.
